questions.stem: Choose the word closest in meaning to ALACRITY:
questions.explanation: Alacrity = brisk and cheerful readiness. Antonym is reluctance (the trap here) — PYQ appearances in SSC CGL Tier-1 and SBI PO. Hook: a + L + acrity → 'a lit up hurry'.
questions.subject: Vocabulary

questions.stem: Choose the word closest in meaning to EPHEMERAL:
questions.explanation: Ephemeral = lasting a very short time. Gk. 'ephemeros' = lasting a day. Very high PYQ hit in Banking RC + SSC synonyms. Antonym 'enduring' is the trap.
questions.subject: Vocabulary

questions.stem: Choose the word closest in meaning to UBIQUITOUS:
questions.explanation: Ubiquitous = present everywhere at once. L. 'ubique' = everywhere. Pair with omnipresent (same meaning, different root). Distractor 'ephemeral' tests two high-hit words at once.
questions.subject: Vocabulary

questions.stem: Choose the word closest in meaning to GARRULOUS:
questions.explanation: Garrulous = excessively talkative, especially on trivial topics. Synonym: loquacious. Antonyms reticent and taciturn sit among the distractors — a textbook test of the cluster.
questions.subject: Vocabulary

questions.stem: Choose the word closest in meaning to PROFLIGATE:
questions.explanation: Profligate = recklessly extravagant, wasteful. The distractor 'generous' is the paper-setter's favourite near-miss — profligate spending is not the same as generous giving.
questions.subject: Vocabulary

questions.stem: Choose the word closest in meaning to OBSEQUIOUS:
questions.explanation: Obsequious = excessively eager to please or obey. Synonyms fawning, sycophantic. Appears repeatedly in Bank PO / SSC CGL vocab. 'Domineering' is its direct antonym — trap.
questions.subject: Vocabulary

questions.stem: Choose the word closest in meaning to MITIGATE:
questions.explanation: Mitigate = to make less severe. Pairs with alleviate, assuage, palliate. Near-twin with 'aggravate' as direct antonym — repeatedly set as a trap pair.
questions.subject: Vocabulary

questions.stem: Choose the word closest in meaning to LACONIC:
questions.explanation: Laconic = using few words, pithy. Origin: Laconia (Sparta), whose people were famously brief of speech. Antonyms verbose, garrulous, loquacious.
questions.subject: Vocabulary

questions.stem: Choose the word closest in meaning to SAGACIOUS:
questions.explanation: Sagacious = shrewd, wise. L. 'sagax' = keen. Pair with astute, prudent, judicious. High-hit in editorials and RC of both SSC and banking.
questions.subject: Vocabulary

questions.stem: Choose the word closest in meaning to CANDID:
questions.explanation: Candid = honest and straightforward. L. 'candidus' = white, pure. Paper-setter's trap: 'reserved' confuses students who think candid means cautious. Genuine antonym is deceitful / secretive.
questions.subject: Vocabulary

questions.stem: Choose the word/phrase closest in meaning to BENEVOLENT:

options.option_text: inclined to do good for others

questions.explanation: BENEVOLENT comes from Latin 'bene' (well) + 'volens' (wishing) — it means wishing or doing good for others (B). Option A (fault-finding) describes a 'censorious' person, which is the opposite in spirit. Option D describes 'malevolent', the direct antonym of benevolent.

questions.stem: Choose the word/phrase closest in meaning to VERBOSE:

options.option_text: given to using too many words
speaking very briefly and to the point
remaining completely silent in all situations
expressing difficult ideas with great precision

questions.explanation: VERBOSE means using more words than necessary; wordy (A). Option B describes 'concise' or 'terse', the direct antonym. Candidates confuse verbose with 'precise' (D) because both relate to language use, but precision is about accuracy, not quantity of words.

questions.stem: Choose the word/phrase closest in meaning to TENACIOUS:

options.option_text: easily swayed by the opinions of others
prone to sudden and unpredictable mood shifts
lacking all confidence in one's own abilities
refusing to yield despite facing all obstacles

questions.explanation: TENACIOUS means holding firmly to a purpose; persistently stubborn (D). It comes from Latin 'tenere' (to hold). Option A ('easily swayed') is the antonym. Candidates often confuse tenacious with 'aggressive', but tenacity is about persistent resolve, not hostility.

questions.stem: Choose the word/phrase closest in meaning to FORTUITOUS:

options.option_text: resulting from meticulous careful advance planning
happening entirely by chance or accident
brought about through sustained personal effort
arising from deeply held moral conviction only

questions.explanation: FORTUITOUS means occurring by chance, not by design (B). A classic SSC trap: the word sounds like 'fortunate' (lucky), so option A ('careful planning') lures candidates who assume it means planned good fortune. Fortuitous is neutral — the event can be lucky or unlucky; only 'chance' is essential.

questions.stem: Choose the word/phrase closest in meaning to ACRIMONIOUS:

options.option_text: bitter and caustic in manner or language
pleasantly warm and openly affectionate always
serenely calm and rational in all disputes
generously giving time without expecting reward

questions.explanation: ACRIMONIOUS describes speech or behaviour that is bitterly harsh (A); from Latin 'acer' (sharp/bitter). It frequently appears in SSC RC passages about political debates. Option B ('warm and affectionate') is the antonym. Option C ('calm and rational') is tempting because disputes can be rational, but acrimony specifically signals emotional bitterness.

questions.stem: Choose the word/phrase closest in meaning to PUGNACIOUS:

options.option_text: eager to avoid all forms of confrontation
showing extraordinary patience under heavy pressure
readily inclined to argue or pick a fight
skilled at persuading others through gentle reason

questions.explanation: PUGNACIOUS means eager to argue or fight; combative (C); from Latin 'pugnus' (fist). This is a frequent banking-exam synonym. Option D ('persuading through reason') is the classic trap because persuasion can involve conflict, but pugnacious implies the desire for combat itself, not rational resolution. Option A is the direct antonym (pacifist tendency).

questions.stem: Choose the word/phrase closest in meaning to RECALCITRANT:

options.option_text: willingly and readily submitting to lawful authority
showing keen eagerness to please one's superiors
obstinately resisting all control or discipline
quickly and smoothly adapting to changing circumstances

questions.explanation: RECALCITRANT means stubbornly disobedient and resistant to authority (C); from Latin 'recalcitrare' (to kick back). It appears in SSC CGL and IBPS PO cloze tests about unruly students or defiant workers. Option A ('submitting to authority') is the antonym. Option D ('adapting to change') is tempting because adaptability and defiance both involve responding to external pressure, but recalcitrant specifically means non-compliance, not flexibility.
